gloss: reluctant; unwilling; not in the mood

definitions.gloss: reluctant; unwilling; not in the mood for
definitions.explanation: Expresses a lack of enthusiasm or willingness to do something. Literally 'one's spirit does not advance.' Used when one feels unenthusiastic about an activity without necessarily having a strong reason to refuse.

examples.japanese: あまり{気|き}が{進|すす}まない。
examples.english: I'm not really feeling up to it.

examples.japanese: {飲|の}み{会|かい}に{誘|さそ}われたが、{気|き}が{進|すす}まなかった。
examples.english: I was invited to a drinking party, but I wasn't in the mood.

examples.japanese: {正直|しょうじき}に{言|い}うと、その{仕事|しごと}を{引|ひ}き{受|う}けるのは{気|き}が{進|すす}まないんです。
examples.english: To be honest, I'm reluctant to take on that job.

notes:
One of many {気|き} expressions in Japanese. Always used in the negative — the positive form {気|き}が{進|すす}む is very rare.

USAGE:
A softer, more polite way to express reluctance than directly refusing. Useful when you want to decline without giving a firm "no."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- あまり{気|き}が{進|すす}まない (I'm not really feeling up to it)
- {気|き}が{進|すす}まないけど (I'm reluctant, but...)
- {正直|しょうじき}{気|き}が{進|すす}まない (to be honest, I'm not keen)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {気|き}が{乗|の}らない: not in the mood (close synonym)
- {乗|の}り{気|き}じゃない: not keen on it (more casual)
- やる{気|き}がある: to be willing/motivated (positive counterpart)
